text: An eigenvalue lambda of a linear operator T satisfies T(v)=lambda*v for some nonzero vector v.
provenance: Original formulation and examples of standard mathematics; independently checked from the displayed definition or calculation. Reference context: Gilbert Strang, MIT 18.06 Linear Algebra, https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/18-06-linear-algebra-spring-2010/. No source prose reproduced.

text: A linear operator N is nilpotent if N^k=0 for some positive integer k.
provenance: Original formulation and examples of standard mathematics; independently checked from the displayed definition or calculation. Reference context: Gilbert Strang, MIT 18.06 Linear Algebra, https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/18-06-linear-algebra-spring-2010/. No source prose reproduced.

text: A linear projection P is an operator satisfying P^2=P. Orthogonality is an additional condition, not part of this definition.
provenance: Original formulation and examples of standard mathematics; independently checked from the displayed definition or calculation. Reference context: Gilbert Strang, MIT 18.06 Linear Algebra, https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/18-06-linear-algebra-spring-2010/. No source prose reproduced.

text: For a unit vector u in R^n, the map P(v)=(u dot v)u is an orthogonal projection. It satisfies P^2=P, with image span(u) and kernel u-perpendicular.
provenance: Original formulation and examples of standard mathematics; independently checked from the displayed definition or calculation. Reference context: Gilbert Strang, MIT 18.06 Linear Algebra, https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/18-06-linear-algebra-spring-2010/. No source prose reproduced.

text: The n-by-n matrix with ones on the superdiagonal and zeros elsewhere shifts coordinates. Its nth power is zero, but its (n-1)st power is nonzero.
provenance: Original formulation and examples of standard mathematics; independently checked from the displayed definition or calculation. Reference context: Gilbert Strang, MIT 18.06 Linear Algebra, https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/18-06-linear-algebra-spring-2010/. No source prose reproduced.

text: For x^2+a*x+b, the matrix [[0,-b],[1,-a]] has characteristic polynomial x^2+a*x+b.
provenance: Original formulation and examples of standard mathematics; independently checked from the displayed definition or calculation. Reference context: Gilbert Strang, MIT 18.06 Linear Algebra, https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/18-06-linear-algebra-spring-2010/. No source prose reproduced.

text: Matrix multiplication need not commute: for A=[[0,1],[0,0]] and B=[[0,0],[1,0]], AB=diag(1,0), BA=diag(0,1).
provenance: Original formulation and examples of standard mathematics; independently checked from the displayed definition or calculation. Reference context: Gilbert Strang, MIT 18.06 Linear Algebra, https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/18-06-linear-algebra-spring-2010/. No source prose reproduced.

text: A real matrix need not be diagonalizable: [[1,1],[0,1]] has only one independent eigenvector despite having two rows.
provenance: Original formulation and examples of standard mathematics; independently checked from the displayed definition or calculation. Reference context: Gilbert Strang, MIT 18.06 Linear Algebra, https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/18-06-linear-algebra-spring-2010/. No source prose reproduced.

text: Determinant 1 does not imply the identity matrix: [[1,1],[0,1]] has determinant 1 and changes (0,1) to (1,1).
provenance: Original formulation and examples of standard mathematics; independently checked from the displayed definition or calculation. Reference context: Gilbert Strang, MIT 18.06 Linear Algebra, https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/18-06-linear-algebra-spring-2010/. No source prose reproduced.

text: The sum of invertible matrices can be singular: I and -I are invertible, while I+(-I)=0.
provenance: Original formulation and examples of standard mathematics; independently checked from the displayed definition or calculation. Reference context: Gilbert Strang, MIT 18.06 Linear Algebra, https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/18-06-linear-algebra-spring-2010/. No source prose reproduced.

text: For an m-by-n matrix A and an n-by-p matrix B over the same field, AB is m-by-p and (AB)_{ij}=sum_{k=1}^n A_{ik}B_{kj}. Each column of AB lies in the column space of A.
provenance: Original explanation or example of standard mathematics, checked by derivation or exact arithmetic. Relevant primary reference read: MIT OpenCourseWare, Gilbert Strang, 18.06SC Linear Algebra, Fall 2011, lecture summary (multiplication), https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/18-06sc-linear-algebra-fall-2011/1963da71c4d96e5d14e7939780f79bcc_MIT18_06SCF11_Ses1.3sum.pdf (accessed 2026-10-13). No source prose reproduced; not a dataset import.

text: For matrices A and B with compatible dimensions over a field, (AB)^T=B^T A^T. Transposition reverses the order of the factors.
provenance: Original explanation or example of standard mathematics, checked by derivation or exact arithmetic. Relevant primary reference read: MIT OpenCourseWare, Gilbert Strang, 18.06SC Linear Algebra, Fall 2011, lecture summary (transpose), https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/18-06sc-linear-algebra-fall-2011/33b21afab62ea8df6c7bd241240df60d_MIT18_06SCF11_Ses1.5sum.pdf (accessed 2026-10-13). No source prose reproduced; not a dataset import.

text: If A and B are invertible n-by-n matrices over the same field, (AB)^(-1)=B^(-1)A^(-1): multiplying either way cancels the adjacent inverse pairs.
provenance: Original explanation or example of standard mathematics, checked by derivation or exact arithmetic. Relevant primary reference read: MIT OpenCourseWare, Gilbert Strang, 18.06SC Linear Algebra, Fall 2011, lecture summary (multiplication), https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/18-06sc-linear-algebra-fall-2011/1963da71c4d96e5d14e7939780f79bcc_MIT18_06SCF11_Ses1.3sum.pdf (accessed 2026-10-13). No source prose reproduced; not a dataset import.

text: For any real m-by-n matrix A, its row space and column space have the same dimension, rank(A), even though they lie in R^n and R^m respectively.
provenance: Original explanation or example of standard mathematics, checked by derivation or exact arithmetic. Relevant primary reference read: MIT OpenCourseWare, Gilbert Strang, 18.06SC Linear Algebra, Fall 2011, lecture summary (subspaces), https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/18-06sc-linear-algebra-fall-2011/62a9db9eeab190694d40afe4734068ca_MIT18_06SCF11_Ses1.10sum.pdf (accessed 2026-10-13). No source prose reproduced; not a dataset import.

text: Row reduction preserves row space but can change column space. The matrices [[1,0],[1,0]] and its reduced row echelon form [[1,0],[0,0]] have the same row space; their column spaces are span((1,1)) and span((1,0)).
provenance: Original explanation or example of standard mathematics, checked by derivation or exact arithmetic. Relevant primary reference read: MIT OpenCourseWare, Gilbert Strang, 18.06SC Linear Algebra, Fall 2011, lecture summary (subspaces), https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/18-06sc-linear-algebra-fall-2011/62a9db9eeab190694d40afe4734068ca_MIT18_06SCF11_Ses1.10sum.pdf (accessed 2026-10-13). No source prose reproduced; not a dataset import.

text: For an n-by-n matrix A over a field and a scalar c, det(cA)=c^n det(A), since every row is scaled. For example, det(3I_2)=9, although 3 det(I_2)=3.
provenance: Original explanation or example of standard mathematics, checked by derivation or exact arithmetic. Relevant primary reference read: MIT OpenCourseWare, Gilbert Strang, 18.06SC Linear Algebra, Fall 2011, lecture summary (determinants), https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/18-06sc-linear-algebra-fall-2011/5dd3f8ec0a398fd74264fef3fd591f81_MIT18_06SCF11_Ses2.5sum.pdf (accessed 2026-10-13). No source prose reproduced; not a dataset import.

text: The determinant is not additive on matrices: with A=B=I_2, det(A+B)=det(2I_2)=4, while det(A)+det(B)=2.
provenance: Original explanation or example of standard mathematics, checked by derivation or exact arithmetic. Relevant primary reference read: MIT OpenCourseWare, Gilbert Strang, 18.06SC Linear Algebra, Fall 2011, lecture summary (determinants), https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/18-06sc-linear-algebra-fall-2011/5dd3f8ec0a398fd74264fef3fd591f81_MIT18_06SCF11_Ses2.5sum.pdf (accessed 2026-10-13). No source prose reproduced; not a dataset import.

text: For A of size m-by-n and B of size n-by-m over the same field, trace(AB)=trace(BA). Both traces equal sum_{i=1}^m sum_{j=1}^n A_{ij}B_{ji}, although AB and BA can have different sizes.
provenance: Original explanation or example of standard mathematics, checked by derivation or exact arithmetic. Relevant primary reference read: MIT OpenCourseWare, Gilbert Strang, 18.06SC Linear Algebra, Fall 2011, lecture summary (multiplication), https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/18-06sc-linear-algebra-fall-2011/1963da71c4d96e5d14e7939780f79bcc_MIT18_06SCF11_Ses1.3sum.pdf (accessed 2026-10-13). No source prose reproduced; not a dataset import.

text: An n-by-n matrix over a field F with n distinct eigenvalues in F is diagonalizable over F. Eigenvectors from distinct eigenvalues are linearly independent and therefore form a basis.
provenance: Original explanation or example of standard mathematics, checked by derivation or exact arithmetic. Relevant primary reference read: MIT OpenCourseWare, Gilbert Strang, 18.06SC Linear Algebra, Fall 2011, lecture summary (similarity), https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/18-06sc-linear-algebra-fall-2011/6e1f793f6c25fd39e002c100e278bf1b_MIT18_06SCF11_Ses3.4sum.pdf (accessed 2026-10-13). No source prose reproduced; not a dataset import.

text: Over R, I_2 and [[1,1],[0,1]] have the same characteristic polynomial (x-1)^2 but are not similar. Every conjugate S^(-1)I_2 S is I_2 itself.
provenance: Original explanation or example of standard mathematics, checked by derivation or exact arithmetic. Relevant primary reference read: MIT OpenCourseWare, Gilbert Strang, 18.06SC Linear Algebra, Fall 2011, lecture summary (similarity), https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/18-06sc-linear-algebra-fall-2011/6e1f793f6c25fd39e002c100e278bf1b_MIT18_06SCF11_Ses3.4sum.pdf (accessed 2026-10-13). No source prose reproduced; not a dataset import.

text: Every real symmetric n-by-n matrix A can be written A=Q D Q^T, where Q is real orthogonal and D is real diagonal. Thus even repeated eigenvalues admit an orthonormal basis of eigenvectors.
provenance: Original explanation or example of standard mathematics, checked by derivation or exact arithmetic. Relevant primary reference read: MIT OpenCourseWare, Gilbert Strang, 18.06SC Linear Algebra, Fall 2011, lecture summary (symmetric), https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/18-06sc-linear-algebra-fall-2011/804ab1e53134741d2044d241b50a285e_MIT18_06SCF11_Ses3.1sum.pdf (accessed 2026-10-13). No source prose reproduced; not a dataset import.

text: A real n-by-n matrix Q is orthogonal when Q^T Q=I. It preserves Euclidean inner products because (Qx)^T(Qy)=x^T y, so it preserves lengths and angles as well.
provenance: Original explanation or example of standard mathematics, checked by derivation or exact arithmetic. Relevant primary reference read: MIT OpenCourseWare, Gilbert Strang, 18.06SC Linear Algebra, Fall 2011, lecture summary (orthogonal), https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/18-06sc-linear-algebra-fall-2011/7ac32be444c25e48590f47573833ccc6_MIT18_06SCF11_Ses2.4sum.pdf (accessed 2026-10-13). No source prose reproduced; not a dataset import.

text: A positive determinant does not imply positive definiteness, even for a real symmetric matrix. A=diag(-2,-3) has det(A)=6, but x^T A x=-2 for x=(1,0).
provenance: Original explanation or example of standard mathematics, checked by derivation or exact arithmetic. text: For a real m-by-n matrix A, its Gram matrix A^T A is symmetric positive semidefinite: x^T A^T A x=||Ax||^2 >= 0. It is positive definite exactly when the columns of A are linearly independent.
provenance: Original explanation or example of standard mathematics, checked by derivation or exact arithmetic. text: Singular values of a real square matrix need not be the absolute values of its eigenvalues. N=[[0,2],[0,0]] has eigenvalues 0,0, while N^T N=diag(0,4) gives singular values 2,0.
